items.title: iconpilot
items.text:
Deterministic tooling + state for designing consistent SVG icon packs.

The AI agent running the skill (Claude, pi, any harness) is the model layer — it drafts variants, screens renders, and drives the loop. iconpilot never calls an LLM: no API keys, no model adapters. It validates, gates, hashes, composes contact sheets, tracks pack state, and exports.

items.title: Why
items.text:
Icon-generation services produce one-off pictures without guarantees. For a production icon pack you need the opposite: a fixed grid, uniform stroke, lint-clean sources, sprite-ready exports, and a human deciding every round. iconpilot makes the machine do the checking:

  • Deterministic gate — parse, lint, geometry, render, similarity; LLMs never self-certify.
  • Human rounds — variants narrow 4 → 2 → 1; you approve/keep/reject via a review page or compact decision text.
  • Pack state — briefs, variants, styles, links, anchors, and statuses in one validated pack.json; exports are always regenerated from source.

items.title: The one-minute tour
items.text:
iconpilot new ~/packs/alpine
iconpilot add ~/packs/alpine hut --brief "Alpine hut: steep roof, small door"
iconpilot check ~/packs/alpine
iconpilot context ~/packs/alpine --icon hut --variant mono   # drafting contract
iconpilot gate ~/packs/alpine/.runs/r001 --pack ~/packs/alpine
iconpilot decide ~/packs/alpine --text 'hut/mono: a1 ok'
iconpilot export ~/packs/alpine --target maplibre --out sprites/

items.text:

  • Library API — embed iconpilot in your build (Django, deploy)

items.title: CLI reference
items.text: All commands accept <pack> as a pack directory or a pack.json path. Everything is non-interactive by default; JSON where useful.

items.title: Pack lifecycle
items.text: Command Purpose iconpilot new <dir> [--name N] Scaffold spec + empty registry (refuses to overwrite) iconpilot add <pack> <icon> --brief "…" [--variant mono:mono-line …] Add an icon with authored variants (todo); repeatable --variant name:style iconpilot check <pack> Full validation: JSON schema, semantics, style resolution, links, DAG iconpilot status <pack> Per-variant states, links, requests, rev, rounds

items.title: The loop
items.text: Command Purpose iconpilot context <pack> --icon I --variant V [--json] Deterministic drafting contract (brief, style, gate thresholds, anchor/reference SVGs) iconpilot gate <run-dir> --pack P Batch-gate every candidate under <run-dir>/<variant>/<icon>/<cand>.svg; writes <cand>.gate.json beside each iconpilot gate <file>.svg --pack P [--variant V] Gate a single SVG (hand tweaks, debugging) iconpilot contact-sheet <dir> --pack P [--out F] One PNG grid of candidates or approved icons iconpilot similar <file> --pack P [--threshold 8] Rank pack SVGs by phash hamming distance; ≤ threshold flagged as link candidates iconpilot decide <pack> --text "…" \| --file F [--round R] Apply decisions (see the loop); the only writer of state transitions

items.title: Review page
items.text: Command Purpose iconpilot review <pack> [--host H] [--port P] Live review server: candidate ok/keep/no, decision text, per-icon editing (brief/prompt/main_color), renders, rev polling

items.title: Export & registry
items.text: Command Purpose iconpilot export <pack> --target T --out DIR svg · sprite-svg · maplibre (@1x/@2x PNG+JSON) · iconify (aliases for links) iconpilot styles [--pack P] Inspect the style registry: built-ins, user config, pack-local iconpilot install-skill [--force] Symlink the skill (SKILL.md + craft.md) into ~/.agents/skills/iconpilot (+ ~/.claude/skills)

items.title: Exit codes
items.text: 0 success · 1 gate/validation failure · 2 usage/parse error · 423 pack locked by another writer (server).

items.title: Packs
items.text: A pack is a directory with pack.json (schema v2) plus icon originals. The pack is the unit of consistency: one grid, one stroke family, one style point per variant. Consuming projects link a pack and export from it.

items.title: Variants are siblings, not derivations
items.text:
An icon has a brief (what it is), an optional prompt (composition hints), an optional main_color, and independently authored variants:

"hut": {
  "brief": "Alpine hut: steep roof, small door, no chimney",
  "main_color": "#346751",
  "variants": {
    "primitive": { "style": "primitive", "anchor": true },
    "mono":      { "style": "mono-line" },
    "color":     { "style": "lineal-color", "reference": "hut#mono" }
  }
}

A primitive is a redraw at lower detail — not a mono with fills flipped. A color variant is a redraw at higher detail. Each variant has its own rounds, status, and decisions.

items.title: anchor and reference
items.text:
• anchor: true — the family form baseline. Its approved SVG is injected into every sibling's drafting context.
  • reference: "<icon>#<variant>" — an additional sibling to visually match.

Both are dependency edges: the pack loader verifies acyclicity, and when an approved target changes, dependents become stale automatically.

items.title: links
items.text:
"selfhut": { "variants": { "primitive": { "link": "hut#primitive" } } }

A variant-level alias: no own file, no own state — it inherits the master's status and materializes at export under its own icon name. Links on non-mono styles require equal main_color on both icons (linked paint must be sound). unlink re-materializes a copy as in_review so it can diverge.

items.title: Styles — one definition, two jobs
items.text:
A style carries gate thresholds and prompt vocabulary:

Axis Values construction outline · solid · outline+fill · hand-drawn color mode mono · bicolor · color · gradient weight thin (1.5) · regular (2) · bold (2.5) detail low · medium · high → node budget, min gap

Three tiers, highest wins: built-ins shipped with the tool (primitive, mono-line, mono-line-thin, mono-bold, filled, duotone, lineal-color, flat-color, gradient-color) < user registry (~/.config/iconpilot/styles.toml) < pack-local (pack.json.styles). Unknown style ids are load errors — register or fix, never invent.

items.title: State machine
items.text:
todo → drafting → in_review → approved (frozen)
                     │  ↑            │
                     └──┘ (keep)     └→ stale (a dependency changed)
         restart (explicit) → todo    reopen (explicit user action)
  • Round state lives per variant; icon-level status is derived, never stored.
  • iconpilot decide is the only writer of state transitions — from the review page or from compact text, the same code path.
  • Approval is always the user's action. Packs created by an LLM (provenance.created_by: "designer") must be todo-only — the validator enforces it.

items.title: Two-layer output
items.text:
Layer Path Editable Originals icons/<icon>/<variant>.svg — readable source of truth by hand, freely — the gate re-validates Assets export/ — optimized SVG, sprites, Iconify JSON never — always regenerated

Kept/approved candidates materialize into icons/ immediately, so the next round (and your hand-tweaks) always start from the current best file.

items.title: The write path
items.text: pack.json has exactly two sanctioned writers: the CLI and the review server (atomic writes + advisory flock, monotonic rev). Decisions flow through decisions.json → decide; live page editing patches per-icon fields only — global spec numbers stay CLI-side so past gate results can't be silently invalidated.

items.title: Improving existing packs
items.text:
Packs often start as an imported baseline — icons already shipped elsewhere (a sprite dir, a previous project, a PR). The import pattern:

"variants": {
  "mono": { "style": "import-mono", "status": "approved",
            "chosen": { "run": "pr314", "variant": "source" } }
}

with transitional styles (import-*) whose notes say what to converge toward, and provenance.source recording where the baseline came from.

items.title: The improve loop
items.text:
1. Reopen exactly what you want to improve — approval is only undone explicitly:
iconpilot decide <pack> --text 'hut/mono: restart "align to new style family"'

The variant goes back to todo; the current SVG stays in icons/ as the refinement base; comments and rejected ideas carry forward.

  1. Point at a target style — swap the transitional import style for a built-in (mono-line, lineal-color, …). Style references are structural metadata: edit them, then iconpilot check.

  2. Run normal rounds — context now emits the target style's thresholds and vocabulary, plus approved siblings as references. Drafts evolve from the imported SVG, not from zero.

  3. Hand-tweaks count — edit the SVG and re-gate; small fixes never need a round.

items.title: Rules of thumb
items.text:
• Never bulk-reopen: improve one variant at a time; the set stays shippable.
  • The gate is informative on approved imports too — run it over icons/ to get a work list of real inconsistencies (bbox overshoot, node counts, near-duplicates via iconpilot similar).
  • Dependent variants (anchor/reference targets) go stale automatically when an approved target changes — let the state machine drive what needs a second look, not your memory.

items.title: Library API
items.text:
iconpilot is a plain Python package with no CLI coupling — embed it in build steps, management commands, or deploy pipelines.

uv add iconpilot --git https://github.com/burgdev/iconpilot.git

Everything public is importable from the package root:

from iconpilot import (
    load_pack, run_gate, build_context,
    collect_exportables, export_maplibre, export_iconify,
)

items.title: Load and validate
items.text:
from pathlib import Path
from iconpilot import load_pack, PackError

try:
    pack, styles = load_pack(Path("iconpacks/accommodation/pack.json"))
except PackError as e:
    ...  # schema + semantic errors, one per line

Raises PackError with all problems (JSON schema shape, style resolution, link targets, DAG cycles), never just the first.

items.title: Gate an SVG
items.text:
from iconpilot import run_gate

report = run_gate("candidate.svg", pack, styles["mono-line"])
report.passed      # bool
report.errors      # ["geometry: 47 nodes > style max 40 (mono-line)", …]
report.checks      # what passed
report.metrics     # {"node_count": 47, "bbox": [...], "ink_ratio": {...}, "phash": "…"}

items.title: Export from source (the "commit only sources" pattern)
items.text:
Commit iconpacks/<pack>/ (pack.json + icons/); generate everything else at build time into ignored directories:

from pathlib import Path
from iconpilot import load_pack, collect_exportables, export_maplibre

repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
pack_dir = repo / "iconpacks" / "accommodation"
pack, _ = load_pack(pack_dir / "pack.json")
entries, skipped = collect_exportables(pack_dir, pack)   # approved + approved links
export_maplibre(entries, repo / "martin_sync/sprites/accommodation", size=48)

As a Django management command this regenerates sprites on deploy; the Entry dataclass tells you what each export came from (master is set when an entry materialized through a link).

items.title: Similarity & context
items.text:
from iconpilot import hash_file, hamming, build_context, render_markdown

if hamming(hash_file("a.svg"), hash_file("b.svg")) <= 8:
    ...  # near-duplicate → suggest a link (human confirms intent)

ctx = build_context(pack_dir, pack, styles, "hut", "mono")
prompt = render_markdown(ctx)   # feed verbatim to a drafting model

items.title: API index
items.text:
Symbol Purpose load_pack, revalidate, schema_errors, PackError load + validate packs Style, BUILTIN_STYLES, resolve_styles, validate_pack style registry & semantics run_gate, GateReport deterministic gate render_png, hash_file, hamming, perceptual_hash, ink_ratio, contact_sheet renders & similarity build_context, render_markdown drafting contracts parse_decision_text, apply_decisions decision grammar & state machine collect_exportables, Entry, export_svg, export_sprite_svg, export_maplibre, export_iconify, tidy exports

No stability guarantees before 1.0; pin your git dependency.

items.title: The agent loop
items.text:
iconpilot is agent-driven: the AI (with the iconpilot skill loaded) is the drafter, the screener, and the orchestrator. The CLI is deterministic tools + state. One round:

1. CONTEXT   iconpilot context <pack> --icon hut --variant mono
2. DRAFT     agent writes candidates to .runs/<round>/<variant>/<icon>/<cand>.svg
3. GATE      iconpilot gate .runs/<round> --pack <pack>     (writes .gate.json)
4. SCREEN    iconpilot contact-sheet .runs/<round> --pack <pack>
5. DECIDE    the user approves/keeps/rejects (page or text) → iconpilot decide
6. REPEAT    until every variant is approved → iconpilot export

items.title: Roles, mapped to your harness
items.text:
Role Realization drafter cheapest capable model you can spawn; feed it the context output verbatim screener any vision-capable model, shown the contact-sheet PNG reviewer / advisor your strongest model, on the whole sheet (set consistency) or for twice-rejected icons designer the agent writing briefs — then iconpilot check

Craft guidance for every drafting model: read craft.md (shipped beside the skill) — grid, stroke discipline, 16px legibility, silhouette-first.

items.title: Decision grammar
items.text:
One icon per line (multiple icons may share a line, separated by · or ;):

hut/mono: a2 keep "thinner roof" · b1 no · more 2
lake/mono: a1 ok
peak/color: * no · restart "too abstract"
Item Effect <cand> ok ["c"] approve → materialize to icons/, freeze <cand> keep ["c"] materialize as working copy, stays in_review <cand> no ["c"] drop candidate * no reject all → back to todo more <N> / like <cand> <N> recorded request for the next round restart ["note"] back to concept; comments + rejected ideas carry forward note "text" icon-level comment

<variant> defaults to the icon's single non-approved variant, else mono. The CLI is the only parser — agents pass user text through verbatim.

items.title: Hand-tweaking between rounds
items.text:
icons/*.svg are yours: edit in Inkscape, VS Code, or an agent, then

iconpilot gate icons/hut/mono.svg --pack <pack>

Small fixes never need a full round; the next drafting pass refines from your edited file.

items.title: Install
items.text:
uv tool install --from git+https://github.com/burgdev/iconpilot.git iconpilot
iconpilot install-skill   # link the skill for your agents (~/.agents/skills)

Python ≥ 3.12. No API keys — models are provided by the agent harness, not this tool.

items.title: Create a pack
items.text:
iconpilot new ~/packs/alpine
iconpilot add ~/packs/alpine hut --brief "Alpine hut: steep roof, small door, no chimney" \
    --variant primitive:primitive --variant mono:mono-line --variant color:lineal-color
iconpilot check ~/packs/alpine

A pack is a plain directory — keep it wherever your project keeps design assets:

alpine/
  pack.json        # spec + icons + state (written by the CLI only)
  icons/hut/*.svg  # originals — hand-editable between rounds
  .runs/r001/      # candidates + gate reports (gitignored)
  export/          # regenerated assets — never hand-edited

items.title: Gate an SVG
items.text:
The gate is deterministic and needs no models:

iconpilot gate my-icon.svg --pack ~/packs/alpine

  ✓ parse: well-formed, single <svg> root
  ✓ viewBox: 0 0 24 24 matches spec
  ✓ lint: elements/attributes conform to style 'mono-line'
  ✓ geometry: bbox inside live area; 16/40 nodes
  ✓ render: [16, 24, 48]px ok (ink 16px=33.6%, …; hash@48px)

items.title: Run a round (with your agent)
items.text:
In any agent session (the iconpilot skill is installed):

"run an iconpilot round on hut/mono"

The agent will:

  1. iconpilot context … --icon hut --variant mono — the deterministic drafting contract (brief, style vocabulary, gate thresholds, anchors)
  2. write candidates to .runs/r001/mono/hut/a1.svg …
  3. iconpilot gate .runs/r001 --pack … — fix until survivors pass
  4. iconpilot contact-sheet .runs/r001 --pack … — screen visually
  5. hand you the decision: review page or compact text
iconpilot decide ~/packs/alpine --text 'hut/mono: a2 keep "thinner roof" · b1 no · more 2'

Approval is always your action. Rinse until every variant is approved.

items.title: Export
items.text:
iconpilot export ~/packs/alpine --target maplibre --out sprites/   # sprite @1x/@2x
iconpilot export ~/packs/alpine --target iconify --out dist/       # collection JSON

Approved variants (and links to approved masters) materialize per icon name; nothing approved means nothing exported — check iconpilot status.
